requirements.quote:
Both the TTL data for RRs and the timing data for refreshing activities
depends on 32 bit timers in units of seconds.
requirements.required_behavior: Use 32-bit timer values for RR TTL data.
requirements.why_checkable: The TTL representation and supported timer width can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
Both the TTL data for RRs and the timing data for refreshing activities
depends on 32 bit timers in units of seconds.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret RR TTL values in seconds.
requirements.why_checkable: A known TTL can be compared with elapsed seconds to check its unit.

requirements.quote:
Both the TTL data for RRs and the timing data for refreshing activities
depends on 32 bit timers in units of seconds.
requirements.condition: Representing timing data for refreshing activities.
requirements.why_checkable: The refresh timer representation and supported timer width can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
Both the TTL data for RRs and the timing data for refreshing activities
depends on 32 bit timers in units of seconds.
requirements.condition: Interpreting timer values for refreshing activities.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret refresh timer values in seconds.
requirements.why_checkable: The refresh interval can be compared with elapsed seconds to check its unit.

requirements.quote:
Inside the database,
refresh timers and TTLs for cached data conceptually "count down", while
data in the zone stays with constant TTLs.
requirements.condition: Time elapses while refresh timers are maintained inside the database.
requirements.required_behavior: Make the remaining refresh interval conceptually count down as time elapses.
requirements.why_checkable: Advancing the clock must reduce the remaining refresh interval; literal decrementing storage is not required.

requirements.quote:
Inside the database,
refresh timers and TTLs for cached data conceptually "count down", while
data in the zone stays with constant TTLs.
requirements.condition: Time elapses while cached RR data is maintained inside the database.
requirements.required_behavior: Make cached-data TTLs conceptually count down as time elapses.
requirements.why_checkable: Advancing the clock must reduce cached data remaining lifetime, regardless of its internal representation.

requirements.quote:
Inside the database,
refresh timers and TTLs for cached data conceptually "count down", while
data in the zone stays with constant TTLs.
requirements.condition: Time elapses while RR data remains in a zone.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the TTLs of data in the zone constant as time elapses.
requirements.why_checkable: Zone TTLs can be compared before and after clock advancement without changing the zone data.

requirements.quote:
A recommended implementation strategy is to store time in two ways:  as
a relative increment and as an absolute time.
requirements.condition: Selecting an internal time-storage implementation strategy.
requirements.required_behavior: It is recommended to support both relative-increment and absolute-time representations.
requirements.why_checkable: The internal timer representations can be inspected for this recommended design choice.

requirements.quote:
A recommended implementation strategy is to store time in two ways:  as
a relative increment and as an absolute time.  One way to do this is to
use positive 32 bit numbers for one type and negative numbers for the
other.
requirements.condition: Choosing the optional sign-based encoding for the recommended relative/absolute time-storage strategy.
requirements.required_behavior: One permitted encoding distinguishes the two time types by using positive 32-bit numbers for one type and negative numbers for the other.
requirements.why_checkable: If this optional encoding is adopted, sign-based time-type discrimination can be inspected; the source does not assign a particular sign to a particular time type.

requirements.quote:
A recommended implementation strategy is to store time in two ways:  as
a relative increment and as an absolute time.  One way to do this is to
use positive 32 bit numbers for one type and negative numbers for the
other.  The RRs in zones use relative times; the refresh timers and
cache data use absolute times.
requirements.condition: Following the recommended strategy that stores time as relative increments and absolute times.
requirements.required_behavior: Use relative times for RRs in zones as part of this recommended strategy.
requirements.why_checkable: The stored time representation for zone RRs can be inspected when evaluating the recommended strategy.

requirements.quote:
A recommended implementation strategy is to store time in two ways:  as
a relative increment and as an absolute time.  One way to do this is to
use positive 32 bit numbers for one type and negative numbers for the
other.  The RRs in zones use relative times; the refresh timers and
cache data use absolute times.
requirements.condition: Following the recommended strategy that stores time as relative increments and absolute times.
requirements.required_behavior: Use absolute times for refresh timers as part of this recommended strategy.
requirements.why_checkable: The stored refresh timer representation can be inspected when evaluating the recommended strategy.

requirements.quote:
A recommended implementation strategy is to store time in two ways:  as
a relative increment and as an absolute time.  One way to do this is to
use positive 32 bit numbers for one type and negative numbers for the
other.  The RRs in zones use relative times; the refresh timers and
cache data use absolute times.
requirements.condition: Following the recommended strategy that stores time as relative increments and absolute times.
requirements.required_behavior: Use absolute times for cached data as part of this recommended strategy.
requirements.why_checkable: The stored cached-data time representation can be inspected when evaluating the recommended strategy.

requirements.quote:
A recommended implementation strategy is to store time in two ways:  as
a relative increment and as an absolute time.  One way to do this is to
use positive 32 bit numbers for one type and negative numbers for the
other.  The RRs in zones use relative times; the refresh timers and
cache data use absolute times.  Absolute numbers are taken with respect
to some known origin and converted to relative values when placed in the
response to a query.
requirements.condition: Using absolute-time numbers under the recommended time-storage strategy.
requirements.required_behavior: Take absolute-time numbers with respect to a known time origin.
requirements.why_checkable: The absolute-time representation can be checked for an identified origin used in its computations.

requirements.quote:
A recommended implementation strategy is to store time in two ways:  as
a relative increment and as an absolute time.  One way to do this is to
use positive 32 bit numbers for one type and negative numbers for the
other.  The RRs in zones use relative times; the refresh timers and
cache data use absolute times.  Absolute numbers are taken with respect
to some known origin and converted to relative values when placed in the
response to a query.
requirements.condition: Placing an internally stored absolute-time value in a query response under the recommended time-storage strategy.
requirements.required_behavior: Convert the absolute-time value to a relative value before placing it in the query response.
requirements.why_checkable: A response generated from an absolute stored expiration can be inspected for a relative remaining lifetime.

requirements.quote:
When an absolute TTL is negative after conversion
to relative, then the data is expired and should be ignored.
requirements.condition: An absolute TTL has been converted to a relative value and the resulting value is negative.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the associated data as expired.
requirements.why_checkable: A stored expiration earlier than the current time can be checked for expired classification after conversion.

requirements.quote:
When an absolute TTL is negative after conversion
to relative, then the data is expired and should be ignored.
requirements.condition: An absolute TTL has been converted to a relative value and the resulting value is negative.
requirements.required_behavior: The expired data should be ignored.
requirements.why_checkable: The use of data whose converted remaining lifetime is negative can be inspected to evaluate the stated recommendation.
